key_insight: Conventional amplitude encoding makes nonzero real-scaled inputs indistinguishable, but a fixed nonlinear feature map removes this ambiguity while preserving logarithmic qubit scaling.
engineering_relevance: The encoding addresses an information bottleneck that downstream quantum circuits cannot fix, without adding trainable parameters.
method: Establish an architecture-independent restriction caused by normalization-induced scale invariance.
Derive a condition for deterministic preprocessing to remove ambiguity; nonlinearity alone is insufficient.
Construct a fixed nonlinear feature map that distinguishes all real inputs after amplitude encoding.
evidence_signal: Across three canonical classification benchmarks and one nonlinear synthetic dataset, the abstract reports 21–44% accuracy improvements over amplitude- and angle-encoding baselines, with a classical neural network also evaluated.
watch_item: Logarithmic qubit scaling does not establish efficient state preparation; practical encoding costs and hardware performance remain unspecified in the abstract.
paper_title: Overcoming the Representational Limitations of Amplitude Encoding for Quantum Neural Networks
